runbooks.title: Known issue: pip install fails in python-fips images [illustrative]
runbooks.body:
Symptom: pip install fails inside python-fips with ValueError: [digital envelope routines] unsupported, or an error mentioning md5.

Cause: some packages call hashlib.md5() during install or import without passing usedforsecurity=False. In FIPS mode, OpenSSL rejects MD5 for security use, so the call raises.

Fix, preferred: build in the standard python image and copy the installed packages into the python-fips runtime image with a multi-stage Dockerfile:
```
FROM registry.echo.ai/python:3.12 AS build
RUN pip install --prefix=/install -r requirements.txt

FROM registry.echo.ai/python-fips:3.12
COPY --from=build /install /usr/local
```
Fix, alternative: upgrade the failing package if a newer release passes usedforsecurity=False.

Do not disable FIPS mode in the runtime image. It defeats the reason the customer chose the FIPS image.

If the error happens at import time in the runtime image rather than at install, the package itself is not FIPS compatible. Escalate with the package name and version.

Tracking issue: echo-images#412.

runbooks.title: Rotating a customer's registry pull tokens [illustrative]
runbooks.body: Internal only. To rotate a customer's pull tokens, open the tenant in the backoffice, revoke tokens older than 90 days, and notify the customer's admin contact before revoking. Never paste tokens in Slack.

runbooks.title: Escalation runbook: customer reports a CVE in an Echo image [illustrative]
runbooks.body: Internal only. When a customer reports a CVE in an Echo image: confirm the image digest, check the patch changelog, and if no patch is published, open an urgent escalation tagged security. Do not give the customer a patch date unless engineering has committed to one in the ticket.
